title: The Orchard content lifecycle
summary: How discovery, currency inspection, and content requests move through two approval gates, publication, platform release, site deployment, and live verification.
description: Three intake paths share one proposal queue. Gate 1 grants permission to author, while Gate 2 approves one exact reviewed revision. Merge, package release, learner-site pinning, and observed live behavior remain separate evidence-bearing steps.
fictionNotice: The completed dossier and browser exercise in this lesson are fictional. Their visibly fictional identifiers demonstrate recordkeeping but are not evidence of a real Orchard production deployment.
actualStatus: In the supplied operator observation dated 2026-09-20, request intake was implemented and the inspected workflow run completed.

The retained request-intake artifact contained an empty opportunities list. This establishes that the inspected path ran, not that any request was approved, authored, published, deployed, or observed live.
The inspected currency workflow materialized a pinned canonical corpus. Observation of that pinned corpus does not establish that every upstream source byte was freshly fetched.

No real production trace covering intake, Gate 1, authoring, review, Gate 2, merge, package release, site pinning, and rendered live verification was supplied. Real completed production lifecycle evidence remains separately required.
diagramLabel: Native visual inventory of all Orchard lifecycle nodes and canonical connections
textAlternativeLabel: Read the complete lifecycle as text
textAlternative: Discovery on the first of each month, currency inspection on the fifteenth, and a labeled content request each enter the shared proposal queue. The queue reaches Gate 1. A no decision ends at No authoring authority. A yes decision links the work item, then research and authoring produce an artifact. Factual and assessment review follows. A failed review goes to correction and loops back to authoring. A passed review reaches Gate 2. A no decision at Gate 2 also goes to correction. A yes decision opens a content pull request. The pull request is validated and merged into canonical content. The platform content package is released separately. The learner site package pin is updated separately. The lesson is then verified live. Failed review, merge, release, or live verification checks each connect to a hold record that retains the reason.

nodes.heading: Discovery: monthly on the 1st
nodes.description: Discovery records candidate sources and concrete eligibility evidence before a proposal reaches the shared queue.

nodes.heading: Currency: monthly on the 15th
nodes.description: Currency inspection records findings against the inspected pinned corpus. Inspecting that corpus alone does not prove that every upstream byte was freshly fetched.

nodes.heading: Labeled content request
nodes.description: Implemented request intake reads structured labeled issues or local fixtures. An empty opportunities artifact shows execution, not completed publication.

nodes.heading: Shared proposal queue
nodes.description: All three intake routes converge here. A queued proposal still lacks authoring authority.

nodes.heading: Approve the proposal?
nodes.description: Gate 1 decides whether authoring may begin. It does not grant publication permission.

nodes.heading: No authoring authority
nodes.description: A Gate 1 denial is a stop. No draft should be commissioned under that denied proposal.

nodes.heading: Link the work item
nodes.description: The approved proposal is linked to a bounded work item so its request, prerequisites, criteria, evidence, decisions, and revisions remain connected.

nodes.heading: Research and author the artifact
nodes.description: The author uses supplied evidence, preserves the authored output as a revision, and keeps claims within the evidence boundary.

nodes.heading: Factual and assessment review pass?
nodes.description: Review checks factual support and whether the assessment can be solved from the lesson. Failure records an exact reason and sends the draft to correction.

nodes.heading: Correct the draft with review findings
nodes.description: Correction creates a new revision and returns it to authoring. A Gate 2 denial uses the same rework route.

nodes.heading: Approve this exact artifact?
nodes.description: Gate 2 binds publication permission to the exact reviewed revision. Editing creates a new revision that requires another review and Gate 2 decision.

nodes.heading: Open a content pull request
nodes.description: The approved revision is proposed to canonical content. Opening a pull request is not a merge, release, deployment, or live observation.

nodes.heading: Validate and merge into canonical content
nodes.description: Canonical checks validate the approved revision before merge. A failed check holds the item with its reason.

nodes.heading: Release the platform content package
nodes.description: Package availability is a separate state after canonical source publication. The package inventory identifies its included content revision.

nodes.heading: Update the learner site package pin
nodes.description: The declared site pin records intended package consumption. Rendered observation is still required because a route or cache may continue to serve older content.

nodes.heading: Verify the lesson is live
nodes.description: Observed behavior requires a rendered check against expected learner text. The fictional dossier includes a stale rendered route, correction, and repeated passing observation.

nodes.heading: Any failed check holds the item with its reason
nodes.description: Review, merge, release, and live verification failures each retain a reason. Resolving one reason does not erase earlier history or unrelated unresolved holds.

Request: FIC-REQUEST-17
Label: content-request
Requested lesson: Explain how an Orchard proposal moves from intake to live verification. Distinguish the two approval gates and preserve separate canonical merge, package release, site pin, and live-observation evidence.

artifacts.label: Fictional dossier
artifacts.title: Prerequisites
artifacts.body:
1. Retain the exact request.
2. Make the canonical lifecycle topology available.
3. Distinguish source publication, package availability, site consumption, and observed behavior.
4. Identify every authored revision without representing a fictional label as a cryptographic digest.

artifacts.label: Fictional dossier
artifacts.title: Acceptance criteria
artifacts.body:
AC1: Show all three intake routes converging on one queue.
AC2: Show Gate 1 denial as no authoring authority.
AC3: Show failed review and Gate 2 denial returning through correction.
AC4: Bind Gate 2 to one exact reviewed revision.
AC5: Keep pull request, canonical merge, package release, site pin, and live verification separate.
AC6: Retain a reason for every failed review, merge, release, or live check.
AC7: Include an assessment that detects an old site pin and missing rendered evidence.

artifacts.label: Fictional dossier
artifacts.title: Supplied excerpts and claim evidence
artifacts.body:
Excerpt A: “Gate 1 authorizes authoring.” Supports the claim that Gate 1 permits drafting.
Excerpt B: “Gate 2 approves this exact artifact.” Supports revision binding.

Excerpt D: “Any failed check holds the item with its reason.” Supports reason-bearing holds.

artifacts.label: Fictional dossier
artifacts.title: Declared learner-site pin
artifacts.body:
Site record: FIC-SITE-PIN-17
Previous declared pin: 4.2.0-fictional.16
Updated declared pin: 4.2.0-fictional.17
Expected rendered text: “Gate 2 approves one exact reviewed revision.”
Expected route content id: orchard-lifecycle
The updated declaration establishes intended consumption only. It does not prove what a rendered route or cache actually served.

artifacts.label: Fictional dossier
artifacts.title: Declared pin versus rendered route
artifacts.body:
Canary: FIC-CANARY-17-A
Declared site pin: 4.2.0-fictional.17
Observed rendered text: “Gate 2 approves publication.”
Expected rendered text: “Gate 2 approves one exact reviewed revision.”
Outcome: FAIL
Hold reason: OLD-SITE-PIN-CACHE. The declaration had changed, but the rendered route still exposed content associated with the previous package.
Corrective action: refresh the fictional route fixture against 4.2.0-fictional.17, clear its stale cache fixture, and repeat the rendered check. The hold clears only after that reason is corrected and reverification passes.

artifacts.title: Reason-bearing hold history
artifacts.body:

Hold FIC-HOLD-17-B: live canary failure on fic-r2, reason OLD-SITE-PIN-CACHE; resolved only after correction of the fictional route fixture and passing reverification FIC-CANARY-17-B.
Both records remain in history after resolution.

Package availability: 4.2.0-fictional.17 inventory contains orchard-lifecycle at fic-r2.

Outcome: FICTIONAL WALKTHROUGH COMPLETE.
This record is not a real production deployment and cannot satisfy the separate real-evidence requirement.

practiceInstructions: Solve each case independently. A solution appears only after you attempt that case. Incorrect choices include causal feedback and can be retried. Completion is earned only when all three cases are correct.

practiceGroups.title: Case 1: Gate 1 denial
practiceGroups.prompt: Gate 1 denies a proposal because its prerequisites do not identify the canonical lifecycle. What may happen next under this decision?
practiceGroups.solution: The denial supplies no authoring authority. The proposal may be corrected and submitted for a new Gate 1 decision, but drafting is not authorized by the denied decision.

practiceGroups.title: Case 2: Edit after Gate 2
practiceGroups.prompt: Gate 2 approved revision fic-r2. An editor then changes assessed wording and saves fic-r3. What is required before opening the content pull request for fic-r3?
practiceGroups.solution: The old review and Gate 2 decision remain historical records about fic-r2 but do not authorize fic-r3. The new revision requires review and a new Gate 2 approval.

practiceGroups.title: Case 3: Merged content, old rendered route
practiceGroups.prompt: Canonical content is merged and the new package exists. The declared site pin was updated, but the rendered route still shows text from the previous package. What is the truthful status?
practiceGroups.solution: The pin declaration and actual rendered result conflict. Keep a live-verification hold, correct the route or cache serving old content, and repeat the rendered check.

choices.label: Begin drafting, but do not publish.
choices.feedback: Incorrect. Gate 1 is the authority to begin authoring. A denial does not permit drafting.

choices.label: Stop authoring work and correct the proposal before seeking a new Gate 1 decision.
choices.feedback: Correct. The denied decision supplies no authoring authority.

choices.label: Skip authoring and ask Gate 2 to publish the request.
choices.feedback: Incorrect. Gate 2 approves an exact reviewed artifact, which does not yet exist.

choices.label: Use the fic-r2 approval because the edit was small.
choices.feedback: Incorrect. Approval is revision-bound. The size of the edit does not make fic-r2 and fic-r3 identical.

choices.label: Review fic-r3 and obtain a new Gate 2 approval bound to fic-r3.
choices.feedback: Correct. The edited artifact requires a new review and exact-revision approval.

choices.label: Merge fic-r3 first and ask reviewers afterward.
choices.feedback: Incorrect. Canonical merge follows review and Gate 2 approval.

choices.label: Complete, because the declared site pin names the new package.
choices.feedback: Incorrect. The rendered route contradicts the declaration, so observed behavior has not passed.

choices.label: Keep a live-verification hold, correct the stale route or cache, and repeat the rendered check.
choices.feedback: Correct. The specific failure reason must be corrected and reverification must pass.

choices.label: Complete, because canonical merge is sufficient.
choices.feedback: Incorrect. Merge does not establish package consumption or rendered behavior.

exercise.heading: Browser-only revision-bound lifecycle exercise
exercise.description: Operate a bounded local state model. It performs no repository, package, deployment, network, or production action. Evidence for review, approval, merge, release, pinning, canary checks, and holds is bound to a revision.
exercise.disclaimer: Simulation only. Button presses change browser memory and do not execute or claim external work.
exercise.expectedText: Gate 2 approves one exact reviewed revision.

actions.label: Grant Gate 1 authority
actions.success: Gate 1 authoring authority was granted for the proposal.

actions.label: Deny Gate 1 authority
actions.success: Gate 1 denied authoring authority. Correcting or reviewing a draft remains blocked until authority is granted.

actions.label: Correct failed draft
actions.success: Created fic-ex-r2. Current-revision derived evidence was reset, while earlier records remained in history.
actions.blocked: Correction requires granted Gate 1 authority and the supplied failed review on fic-ex-r1.

actions.label: Run local review check
actions.success: The current corrected revision passed the local fixture checks.
actions.blocked: Review requires granted Gate 1 authority and a corrected current revision.

actions.label: Bind Gate 2 approval
actions.success: Gate 2 now binds to the current reviewed revision.
actions.blocked: Gate 2 requires a passing review bound to the current revision.

actions.label: Edit after Gate 2
actions.success: Created fic-ex-r3. Current review, approval, merge, release, pin, canary, and hold state was invalidated. Earlier records remain visible in history.
actions.blocked: First create a Gate 2 binding for fic-ex-r2.

actions.label: Validate and merge
actions.success: The current approved revision passed the canonical fixture and was marked merged.
actions.blocked: Merge requires Gate 2 approval bound to the current revision.

actions.label: Release package fixture
actions.success: The package fixture now includes the merged current revision.
actions.blocked: Package release requires a merge bound to the current revision.

actions.label: Update site pin fixture
actions.success: The site fixture now declares the intended package for the current revision.
actions.blocked: Pinning requires a package release bound to the current revision.

actions.label: Run rendered canary fixture
actions.success: Reverification for the current revision found the expected text and resolved its corrected canary hold.
actions.blocked: Verification requires the intended current-revision pin. The first eligible canary for each revision intentionally records OLD-SITE-PIN-CACHE; correct that specific fixture and retry.

actions.label: Correct failed canary fixture
actions.success: The stale route fixture for the current revision was corrected. Its hold remains unresolved until reverification passes.
actions.blocked: Correction is available only for an unresolved OLD-SITE-PIN-CACHE hold bound to the current revision.

exercise.completionText: The exercise is complete only when Gate 1 authority is granted and the current revision is reviewed, approved to that revision, merged, released, pinned, and observed with no unresolved hold.

historyMessages.corrected: Created {revision}; the earlier review and hold remain historical.
historyMessages.edited: Created {revision}; all derived state was invalidated for the new revision.
historyMessages.canaryCorrected: Corrected OLD-SITE-PIN-CACHE for {revision}; reverification remains required.
historyMessages.reverified: Reverification passed for {revision}; its canary hold was resolved.

takeaways: Gate 1 grants authoring authority. Gate 2 grants publication-path authority for one exact reviewed revision.
Changing an artifact invalidates derived authority and evidence for the changed revision while historical records remain visible.
Canonical source publication, package availability, declared site consumption, and observed rendered behavior require separate evidence.
Only correction of a specific hold reason followed by the required reverification may clear that hold.
A fictional walkthrough or browser exercise cannot substitute for a completed production lifecycle trace.
